_comment: HARD GATE — canonical format for every inline Greek/Hebrew gloss in the corpus (discovery + encounters, every language). Enforced by check_greek_hebrew_transliteration / find_greek_hebrew_glosses in shared_validation/text_checks.py. This file is the spec; the Python code reads it rather than hardcoding the rule, so the format can be corrected in one place without touching validator logic. STRICT: exactly two accepted forms, no other conventions, no exceptions.
rule: <original Greek or Hebrew word>,<one ASCII space>(<Latin transliteration>)  OR  <word> <word>,<one ASCII space>(<Latin transliteration>)
example: θεός, (theos)  —  or, for a genuine two-word grammatical phrase  —  τὸ γεγονός, (to gegonos)
explanation: Two accepted forms only: a single native-script word, or a genuine two-word native-script phrase (e.g. article + participle, adverb + participle, construct pair) — never three or more words, never a full sentence.

In both forms: the native-script word(s) first, then an ASCII comma ',' immediately after the last word (no space before the comma), then exactly one ASCII space, then an opening ASCII parenthesis '(' — never a full-width '（' or '，'.

The parenthetical contains ONLY the Latin-alphabet transliteration of the exact same word(s) — never the original script repeated, never a phonetic respelling into the target language's own script (e.g. Chinese 索索, Japanese カタカナ, Arabic script, Devanagari). This has shipped wrong before in AR/HI/JA/ZH — always Latin letters only.

No other form is accepted. No bare reuse of a transliteration without its gloss, no matter how recently the word was introduced in the same field. No full-sentence original/transliteration pairing. Every occurrence of every native-script word or two-word phrase must carry its own gloss, every time.
violations_not_accepted: No space before the parenthesis: θεός,(theos)
Original script repeated inside the parenthetical instead of a transliteration: θεός, (θεός)
Phonetic respelling into the target script instead of Latin: θεός, (泰奥斯)
Bare reuse without a gloss: introducing 'θεός, (theos)' once and later writing bare 'theos' with no gloss
Three-or-more-word phrase or full-sentence original/transliteration pairing instead of a 1-or-2-word gloss

transliteration_charset._comment: The specific Latin-alphabet characters this corpus's transliteration convention actually uses, derived empirically from every well-formed gloss already in the encounters corpus (2026-07-27 scan, 70 samples). NOT the full SBL academic Hebrew table (no ḥ/ṭ/ṣ/ś/š/ʾ/ʿ, no breves ă/ĕ/ŏ, no circumflexes â/î/ô) — this corpus uses a simplified scholarly style: macrons for Greek long vowels (η→ē, ω→ō) and acute-accented vowels for stress, including macron+acute combined forms for a stressed long vowel. A character outside this set (e.g. a Vietnamese/Turkish/Polish Latin letter, or a strict-academic Hebrew emphatic mark not yet used anywhere) is very likely either a mistake or a style the corpus hasn't adopted yet — treat as a flag to review, not a silent pass. Extend this list only after confirming a new mark is intentionally being introduced as house style, the same way this list itself was derived (empirical scan + explicit decision), not by loosening the regex ad hoc.
transliteration_charset.ascii: A-Za-z (plain Latin letters, digits 0-9, and punctuation: space hyphen apostrophe period colon)
